definition: The median: half of cases are faster than this.
90% of cases are faster than this. It shows your slow tail, which is where incidents come from.
The share of what users see that breaks a rule.
Of everything your system acted on, the share that really broke the rules.
Of all the rule-breaking content out there, the share your system caught.
The range the true value probably sits in, given how big your sample was.
Service-level agreement: the response time you've committed to.
A machine-learning model that labels content, for example spam or not spam.
A comparison group chosen to look like the group you're studying, so the main difference is the thing you're measuring.
An organization officially recognized under the EU DSA to report illegal content. Its notices must be handled first.
The explanation the EU DSA requires you to send a user when you restrict their content or account.
People who deliberately attack your system to find weaknesses before real attackers do.
A prompt written to trick an AI into ignoring its safety rules.
Hidden instructions in a document, web page or tool result that try to take control of an AI.
Comparing files against a database of known illegal images by their digital fingerprint.
A banned user coming back with a new account.
When a card issuer reverses a payment, usually because the cardholder disputed it.
Any method of estimating or verifying a user's age, from a typed birth date to an ID check.
One of the few top-level numbers that show whether users are actually safer.
The EU Digital Services Act. It sets rules for how online services handle illegal content, complaints and transparency in the EU.
The UK law that requires online services to assess and reduce the risk of illegal content and, where children are likely to use them, harm to children. Ofcom enforces it.
The UK communications regulator, which enforces the Online Safety Act.
Child sexual abuse material. Illegal to make, possess or share in almost every country. US providers must report it to NCMEC.
NCMEC's system for reports of child sexual exploitation. US providers are required by law to report to it.
The EU General Data Protection Regulation, which governs how personal data is collected, used and kept.
The US Children's Online Privacy Protection Act. It requires verifiable parental consent before collecting personal data from children under 13.
An open model from OpenAI that labels content against a policy you write. Free to download; you run it on your own hardware.
Request for proposal: the document you send vendors asking how they would meet your requirements, and at what price.
Threatening to share someone's intimate images unless they pay or send more. Teenagers are frequent targets.
When an adult builds a child's trust over time in order to sexually abuse or exploit them.
A clear structure for running a crisis: one person in charge, defined roles and a regular rhythm of updates.
Publishing someone's private information, such as their home address, to harass or endanger them.
Moving a case to a more senior or specialist reviewer, such as legal or child safety, because it's severe or unclear.
